result.summary: The image shows an urban residential street with sidewalks on both sides and a marked crosswalk at an intersection controlled by a traffic signal. While basic infrastructure exists, the wide roadway and parked vehicles near the crossing create potential visibility and exposure risks for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the right side of the street extend close to the intersection, potentially obscuring pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, along the curb.

hazards.name: Unprotected Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the full width of the street without a refuge island or curb extensions to shorten the exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: The marked crosswalk area across the main roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Replace the standard transverse lines with continental or ladder-style markings to increase the visibility of the crossing.

result.summary: The image shows a typical urban intersection with marked continental crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and traffic signals are present, the environment lacks advanced safety features like curb extensions or daylighting to improve visibility at the crossing.

hazards.name: Restricted Sightlines (Daylighting)
hazards.description: Parked vehicles are located very close to the crosswalk, potentially obscuring pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection along the curb.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer such as trees or bollards between the sidewalk and the moving traffic lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk edge on both sides of the street.

interventions.description: Install street trees to provide a vertical buffer for pedestrians and naturally calm traffic speeds.

result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection with multi-story brick buildings and basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, traffic signals, and marked crosswalks. While functional, the environment lacks advanced safety features like curb extensions or high-visibility markings to reduce pedestrian exposure.

hazards.name: Standard Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The parallel line markings are less visible to approaching motorists than high-visibility continental patterns.

hazards.name: Unprotected Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the roadway without a median or refuge island.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing parallel line markings to a continental or ladder pattern to increase visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.
